It's inevitable that complete freedom of speech will tend to attract people who needs it to express themselves, and not the people who doesn't need it and is comfortable with their current website. This is not to say that a user who've been banned from Reddit must have been really unpleasant to deal with; there has been a lot of unfair and shady automated banning. But there must have been a lot of reasonable bans too (this might not seem the case because people who share their ban story tend to not put themselves in a negative light, and sympathy = upvotes = exposure).

Reddit did a kind of weeding, a purge so to speak. Most can agree that it was unethical and an affront to the whole idea of free speech. But the nature of the Reddit migration made it really likely that Voat was going to have an imbalance issue. Most users who left Reddit for Voat are probably pleasant and were just sick of Reddit's company decisions. But I think it's safe to say that a majority of toxic users left Reddit for Voat. This might be a small minority of the whole immigration overall, but a small percentage of a really big number is still a big number.
